Aida. Giuseppe Verdi's Aida, composed in 1871, is a grand opera in four acts set in ancient Egypt during a conflict with Ethiopia. Commissioned by Cairo's Khedivial Opera House to celebrate its opening, the opera depicts a tragic love triangle between Radames, a heroic Egyptian military commander; Amneris, the Pharaoh's jealous daughter; and Aida, an enslaved Ethiopian princess. When Radames is chosen to lead the Egyptian army, he is caught between his love for Aida and his loyalty to the Pharaoh, while Aida must choose between her lover and her homeland.

Aida is an Ethiopian princess captured and enslaved as a handmaiden to Amneris. She struggles to balance her love for Radames with her loyalty to her father and country. Radames is the Egyptian captain of the guard chosen by the goddess Isis to lead the war effort against Ethiopia, hoping a victory will allow him to marry Aida. Amneris is the Pharaoh's daughter passionately in love with Radames who orchestrates schemes to confirm Aida's feelings for him, leading to the ultimate tragedy. Amonasro is Aida's father and the King of Ethiopia who disguises his royal status when captured, later pressure-guilting Aida into extracting Egyptian troop movements from Radames.

The opera features several famous pieces. Triumphal March, also called Gloria all'Egitto, is the grand, brass-heavy Act Two instrumental and choral piece celebrating Radames's victorious return with prisoners. Ritorna vincitor, meaning Return victorious, is Aida's conflicted Act One aria in which she realizes she is praying for her lover's victory, which would mean the defeat of her father. O patria mia, or O my homeland, is Aida's Act Three aria reflecting on the beauty of her native country, which she fears she will never see again. O terra, addio, or O earth, farewell, is the serene final duet sung by Aida and Radames as they suffocate inside the dark vault beneath the Temple of Vulcan.

After Radames is tricked into betraying military secrets, he is sentenced to be buried alive. Aida secretly slips into the tomb to join him, and they die together in each other's arms. Giuseppe Verdi was the preeminent composer of nineteenth-century Italian opera.
